subject: Clarify CPRA/CCPA: service provider vs processor + telemetry redline (MedNavigator)
messages:
From: Rachel Owens <rachel.owens@mednavigator.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Markus Bell <markkus.bell@mednavigator.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@mednavigator.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CPRA/CCPA DPA redline – service provider vs processor and telemetry

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking a look. Attached is our DPA redline — the legal team flagged two areas that need clearer alignment for US state privacy: (1) the service provider / processor classification language (we call for explicit "only as a service provider" use limitations), and (2) telemetry/usage data that may be generated during inference (they want assurances that telemetry will not be used for targeted advertising and a transfer boundary where telemetry is considered aggregate only).

Specific asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood will accept an explicit limited-use clause in the US-privacy addendum (we've proposed an addendum paragraph in the attached), and whether the telemetry language can be constrained to aggregate diagnostic metrics only.
- If you need to propose alternative wording, please send a tracked redline by EOD Monday so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Attachments: MedNavigator_DPA_Redline.docx

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

--
Rachel Owens
Director, Legal Operations
MedNavigator Inc.
rachel.owens@mednavigator.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA/CCPA DPA redline – service provider vs processor and telemetry

Rachel — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. Looping in Marissa (contracts) and Aditya (privacy) to vet the precise CPRA/CCPA language you attached. High level: Redwood's platform is offered as a service and we have a narrow telemetry posture for customers (diagnostic metrics, sampling, and optional telemetry opt-out), but we want to align on exact bright-line wording MedNavigator needs to satisfy your procurement.

Next steps:
- Marissa will propose narrowly tailored contractual language that keeps our operational controls (KV cache, prefix caching) intact while addressing the limited-use clause.
- Aditya will confirm the telemetry treatment we can commit to (aggregate/diagnostic only for safety/ops; no use for ad targeting).
- I'll follow up with an annotated redline by Tuesday EOD and propose a 30-minute sync if you prefer to walk through examples.

Thanks —

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA/CCPA DPA redline – proposed language

Vanessa / Aditya — reviewed Rachel's redline. Drafted two short options in the attached RNW_Proposed_CPR_Text.docx:

Option A (Commercially aligned):
- Redwood accepts a "service provider" treatment for customer Content and Customer Personal Data under US state privacy laws, with a limited-use covenant: Redwood will process Customer Personal Data only to provide the services defined in the Agreement, to maintain and improve service reliability (aggregate diagnostics only), and to comply with law. No use for advertising or model training for third-party marketing.

Option B (Narrow, privacy-first):
- Same as A but with an explicit telemetry exclusion clause and a requirement that telemetry be stored only in aggregate with a 90-day retention cap, unless customer opts in to extended retention.

Risk notes (Aditya): please confirm whether the 90-day cap is operationally feasible for ops-debugging across our dedicated pools (we typically keep rolling short-term windows for KV/trace diagnostics).

I'll produce a tracked redline combining Option A with an operational carve that avoids breaking caching/latency functionality. If Aditya can confirm telemetry feasibility by EOD Monday I can send the redline back to MedNavigator.

--
Marissa Cole
Contracts Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-06-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CPRA/CCPA DPA redline – agreed text and DocuSign

Rachel / Vanessa / Marissa — quick update and proposed final: Per our internal checks, we can commit to the following binding operational controls: (1) telemetry limited to aggregated operational metrics; (2) telemetry retention default 90 days with customer opt-in for extended retention; (3) explicit covenant: no use of telemetry or Customer Personal Data for targeted advertising or training third-party marketing models. We will preserve any runtime caching (KV/prefix) required to serve requests, but caching content is scoped to the customer and not used for cross-customer profiling.

Attached: RNW tracked redline with the agreed paragraph inserted. If that aligns, Vanessa — please send to MedNavigator with a DocuSign link.

Attachments: RNW_Proposed_CPR_Text.docx

On behalf of Redwood Inference, I confirm the text below can be inserted into the US-privacy addendum: 

"Redwood Inference shall act as a service provider/processor under applicable US state privacy laws and shall process Customer Personal Data solely to provide the services described in this Agreement and for aggregate diagnostic and security purposes. Redwood will not use Customer Personal Data or any telemetry derived from Customer interactions for targeted advertising, or to train models for third-party marketing. Telemetry will be retained in aggregated form by default for a period of 90 days unless Customer opts in to extended retention. Operational caching required to serve requests may be maintained, but Redwood will not use cached Customer Content to profile or target other customers."

Please confirm and we'll route to DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/abc1234567890

Thanks,

Aditya
